rules.reason: Local Codex/agent configuration is not product source.
Signing material and environment secrets must remain outside release source.

Executable native safety-kernel evidence belongs with the native implementation. integrity/ holds the root-detection probe tests and its device-evidence instrumentation (A-017). security/ holds the overlay (tapjacking) touch-policy decisions, whose gateway-vs-non-gateway split is what keeps the guard from locking an owner out of their own safety app.
JVM evidence for VolumeButtonDetector.kt, which sits at the package root rather than under emergency/. The detector is a panic entry point, so its test ships with the native safety kernel it guards.

Instrumentation evidence that the INSTALLED package declares the flutter_local_notifications scheduled-delivery and boot-reschedule receivers (R5). It proves a manifest declaration, so it travels with the manifest change rather than with the native kernel.

Native emergency state, scheduling, dispatch, and platform-channel authority. VolumeButtonDetector.kt is the native half of the volume-button panic trigger, so it is a safety entry point like the quick-access surfaces. integrity/ is the native root-detection probe (A-017) whose verdict gates the duress-model device warning. security/ owns the overlay touch policy that MainActivity enforces on the PIN, consent, export and reset surfaces.
Evidence that the quick-access surfaces stay intent-only and never share the native pending-trigger key.
Home-screen widget and Quick Settings tile: they submit a panic request and launch the launcher activity; the arm boundary stays in the Flutter path.
Executable Flutter/platform safety behavior evidence.
Stage 4 executable Flutter-to-Android runtime probe; it is test-only evidence and not a production entrypoint.
Flutter safety projection, PIN/session handling, and safety-facing lifecycle code.
Reproducible build wrapper/lock output or generated store media.

Android manifest, R8 keep rules, dependency, toolchain, and build configuration. The debug/play/profile manifests are merged into those variants, so the play one is part of the release manifest surface. key.properties.example is the placeholder-only signing template; the real key.properties stays in secret-quarantine through the earlier rule, which requires the name to END in key.properties.
Android resources that ship in the release surface: system-rendered labels, launcher icon densities, widget layout and its palette mirror.

CI, evidence, security, audit, or release-governance source. SECURITY.md is the published vulnerability-disclosure channel and CHANGELOG.md is the source for the Play 'what's new' text, so both are release governance rather than product source. CLAUDE.md is the checked-in engineering rule set every change is reviewed against (it is tracked, unlike the local-only AGENTS.md and .claude/ tooling). The named docs/*.md files are dated audit, security-design, device-investigation, plan and workflow records.
Candidate-facing legal, Play declaration, billing, QA, or store material.
Legal consent behavior and executable public-claim regression evidence.
Localized product copy or store-asset source.
Translation bundle gates ship in the same commit group as the bundles they guard.

Production-readiness standard and its per-requirement audit, remediation, continuity, resolution-queue, external-blocker, and independent-review outputs are release-governance source. The review pattern is deliberately open-ended on BOTH sides: a NEW reviewer report must never be able to fail the classification gate simply by existing, and FINAL_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md proved a leading qualifier could do exactly that.
Executable degraded-condition evidence: GPS off, low battery, denied permissions, offline queue.

Contacts repository/datasource, location repository, device-security and secure-storage source. Appended LAST on purpose: lib/services/consent_manager.dart and lib/models/consent_record.dart keep the earlier legal classification, because first match wins. Before this rule the gate could not classify lib/services/device_security_service.dart at all -- a security file invisible to a fail-closed gate is the gate failing open.
Bundled Flutter assets: launcher/splash artwork and the siren and fake-call ringtone audio. The siren is a safety surface, so a re-encode ships in the same group as the Flutter code that plays it.
Root .gitignore decides what can enter release source at all (it is what keeps key.properties and keystores out of the index); analysis_options.yaml configures the CI analyze gate.
Written by the Flutter tool (project/migration metadata) and by DevTools; committed so the toolchain state is reproducible, never hand-authored.
